newsitem.title: USA: Embrex will take write-off, sees Q4 loss.
newsitem.headline: Embrex will take write-off, sees Q4 loss.

text.p: Embrex Inc said it will take a $160,000 fourth quarter write-off of obsolete materials, which will create a loss for the fourth quarter.
Embrex reported a loss of $596,000 or $0.09 per share in 1995's fourth quarter.
The company said fourth quarter operations would have been profitable, without the write-off. It said it will report a profit for the 1996 year.
The company also said it received U.S. Department of Agriculture approval for its new viral neutralizing factor-based vaccine for Infectious Bursal Disease (IBD) in broiler chickens.
Embrex said the approval is specifically for in ovo (in-the-egg) administration of the vaccine complex via its patented Inovoject egg injection system.
Currently, 80 percent of the broiler chickens raised in the U.S. and Canada receive certain in ovo vaccines via the Inovoject system.
IBD weakens a chicken's immune system, resulting in poor growth and the potential for contracting other diseases. The disease is widespread in the U.S., Northern Europe and Asia, Embrex said.
